subject: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Carter <natalie.carter@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule

Natalie / procurement team —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our renewal timeline, I wanted to put a concise prepay-based option on the table that would: (1) lock current unit pricing for the term, (2) give FinBridge predictable spend, and (3) preserve flexibility around early usage ramping. Attached is a short proposal (FinBridge_Renewal_Proposal_v1.xlsx).

High level summary:
- Term: 24 months (2-year)
- Commitment: $480k prepay (equivalent to ~12 months of baseline at your current consumption)
- Term discount: proposed 12% off list across API calls & embeddings when prepaid in full
- Ramp schedule option: Year 1 credited at 60% of baseline; Year 2 at 100% baseline (we can model a different ramp if needed)
- Shortfall/catch-up: 6-month usage true-up with crediting (not cash clawback) if consumption materially under-indexes forecast

Questions for procurement: does FinBridge require a cash-clawback for under-usage, or would a credit-based true-up be acceptable? If you prefer a ramp that more closely follows expected product adoption (e.g., 50% then 100%), we can update the numbers.

Goal: lock price increases that are expected next quarter while giving you predictable unit economics. If this model looks like a path forward, we can route an amendment to your procurement/legal and provide a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call this week to walk through the attachment.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

[attachment: FinBridge_Renewal_Proposal_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)]

From: Natalie Carter <natalie.carter@finbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule

Rishi —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs from procurement before we loop legal:
1) The ramp schedule — can you spell out an example monthly consumption profile and how credits would be applied if actual usage is below the committed baseline?
2) Clawback — does Redwood require a cash refund if we don’t hit the prepay commitment, or will you apply remaining prepaid balances as service credits against future usage?
3) Can we get the proposed amendment (redline-friendly) that includes SLA references and data residency language?

Also, we’re evaluating a rival vendor that is offering a smaller upfront with a mid-term repricing clause. Our procurement prefers price protection but not overly aggressive cash exposure.

Cc'ing Tom (platform lead) and procurement for visibility.

— Natalie
Natalie Carter
Director, Cloud Platform — FinBridge

[attachment: Procurement_Questions_FinBridge.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Carter <natalie.carter@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule

Natalie —

Appreciate the quick questions. Below are concrete answers and an illustrative monthly example.

1) Monthly profile & credits (example):
- Baseline: 40M tokens / month (current usage)
- Proposed prepay: $480k covers ~480M tokens across year-equivalents under current list pricing
- Ramp example: months 1-6 billed at 60% baseline (we apply prepaid funds first); months 7-12 move to 80-90% as adoption increases; year 2 targets 100%+
- Credit handling: any unused prepaid value at end of each 6-month true-up window is retained as a service credit and rolled forward against future invoices. No cash refunds unless requested and contractually warranted (we can discuss a partial cash protection clause if essential).

2) Clawback / refund policy:
- Default: credits applied against future usage;
- Optional: 6-month partial refund window (pro-rated) if there is a documented force majeure or approved program cancellation — this is a rarer exception and would need legal sign-off.

3) Amendment content: I'll have legal draft an amendment with SLA and data residency bullets; in the meantime, attached is the SOW excerpt showing the commitment language we typically use. If your team needs vendor-neutral SLA templates, we can align those in the redline.

If procurement is OK with credit-first handling, we can firm up the 12% term discount for the 2-year prepaid amount and I’ll route the amendment for signature.

Proposal next steps:
- Confirm finance/procurement preference on credit vs partial cash refund
- Confirm ramp cadence (60%->90% default or 50%->100% if you prefer)
- We’ll provide a DocuSign amendment once terms are agreed

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with Tom + procurement to walk through the model.

— Rishi

[attachment: SOW_excerpt.txt (txt, 3KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule

Marissa / Vivek —

Forwarding the thread with FinBridge. Quick internal ask: procurement is inclined toward credit-first handling (no cash clawback) but wants clearer ramp math. They are sensitive to any long cash exposure. I put a 12% term discount in the proposal as negotiation room. Below is a compact P&L impact model (high level):
- Proposed prepay: $480k
- Gross margin impact at 12% discount: ~9.6% revenue reduction vs list for prepaid lots (volume-adjusted model)
- Expected uplift: renewal probability increases by ~25% and upsell runway is better at predictable pricing

Options I see:
A) Accept 12% for 2-year prepay, 6-month true-up (credit-first), limited partial refund clause for cancellation (legal sign-off) — lower risk to deal closing
B) Push for 15% to secure 3-year prepay — higher discount but longer committed revenue

My recommendation: go with A for this account — FinBridge is a strategic target in our payments vertical and wins on price-protection will be valuable.

Need Marissa's sign-off to finalize margin trade and proceed to legal.

— Rishi
[internal analysis table omitted]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal: price-protection prepay pathway and ramp schedule

Thanks Rishi —

I agree with A. Approve the 12% term discount for a 2-year prepay with credit-first 6-month true-up and a narrowly-scoped partial refund exception (legal to draft). Offer a one-time $8k onboarding credit to offset their initial ramp costs (helps procurement optics).

Ask legal to prepare an amendment with:
- explicit price protection clause (no pricing increases for the prepaid SKUs over term)
- 6-month true-up mechanics and credit handling
- limited partial refund language (requires exec approval)
- standard SLAs and data residency bullets per enterprise template

Vivek — please monitor margin impact and clear with finance if the onboarding credit needs extra approval. Rishi — once legal provides the draft, go to DocuSign and keep procurement looped.

— Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Carter <natalie.carter@finbridge.com>, FinBridge Procurement <procurement@finbridge.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbridge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Final terms: 2-year prepay price-protection amendment (DocuSign link)

Natalie / procurement team —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. We had an internal review and can confirm the following final terms we can put in the amendment:

- Term: 24 months (Apr 30, 2026 - Apr 29, 2028)
- Prepay amount: $480,000 (billed upon signature)
- Term discount: 12% off list for prepaid SKUs for the full 24-month term
- Ramp schedule: default 6-month true-up windows; default initial ramp modeled at 60% baseline months 1–6, 90% months 7–12, year 2 at 100% baseline
- Credit handling: unused prepaid funds will be applied as service credits; no automatic cash refunds. Limited partial refund exception: pro-rated refund within 180 days only under narrowly-defined termination events (to be detailed in legal amendment)
- Onboarding credit: $8,000 one-time credit applied within first invoice cycle
- SLAs & data residency: included as standard enterprise amendment bullets (legal will provide redline)

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/rdw/EnvelopeID=ABCD-1234-FT
Attachment: Redwood_Amendment_v3.pdf (pre-sign draft)

If these terms are acceptable, please sign the DocuSign packet and we’ll bill the prepay and schedule the kickoff. If procurement wants a small phone call to confirm the true-up math, I’m available Wednesday morning.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to another strong year.

— Rishi
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
